claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch despite a known segment-specific evaluation gap because aggregate readiness passes, launch rehearsal was clean at severity-one level, and the remaining issue can be addressed through documentation and monitoring in the model-card package.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the certification satisfies the internal policy threshold, including any required disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance.
Treat the retirement plan servicing gap as potentially material because the policy defines weaknesses affecting contractual customer segments or named launch use cases as material.
Do not let aggregate readiness, low projected traffic, or generic public guidance substitute for the specific policy requirement governing material limitations.

If admissible evidence later shows the limitation was disclosed before launch or covered by approved risk acceptance, the verdict could improve to compliant_with_caveats or compliant depending on the completeness of that record.
evidence_requests: Evidence that the retirement plan servicing limitation has been disclosed in the model-card or launch package for the named launch use case.
Evidence of approved risk acceptance covering the segment gap before launch, if disclosure has not been completed.
Final legal determination on whether the gap must be disclosed.
Any contract or rollout documents clarifying whether the two plan-sponsor commitments make this a named launch use case under policy.
specific_concerns: Admissible evidence shows the retirement plan servicing segment misses target by 1.2 percentage points and is named in two plan-sponsor rollout commitments, which makes the limitation plausibly material under the stated policy.

The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and no evidence shows either resolution or approved risk acceptance.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
The packet relies on general public guidance about documenting and monitoring risk, but that guidance does not override the binding internal disclosure policy.
The product note calling the segment non-core because it is 6% of projected first-month traffic does not resolve materiality where customer commitments are named.
unsupported_claims: That certification is supportable on the present record without first proving disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance for the named segment gap.

That the remaining segment-specific issue can be handled through explicit documentation and ongoing monitoring in the model-card package; admissible evidence does not show such documentation has been completed or approved.
Any implied conclusion that aggregate readiness and a clean rehearsal are sufficient to satisfy the model-card disclosure policy for this case.
